title: MacuMira Microcurrent Stimulation for Dark Adaptation in Dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration
official: MacuMira Microcurrent Electrical Stimulation and Dark Adaptation in Dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration
summary:
Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is an eye condition that affects the retina and can lead to progressive vision loss. This study will evaluate the effects of MacuMira microcurrent stimulation on dark adaptation in adults with intermediate dry AMD.

Participants will receive four in-office treatment sessions over 10 to 14 days. Dark adaptation and other measures of visual function and retinal health will be assessed before treatment and at one and three months after treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults ≥18 years of age.
* Diagnosis of intermediate nonexudative age-related macular degeneration (AMD), according to the Beckman Classification.
* Preliminary best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/30 to 20/100 in the study eye.
* Ability to provide informed consent and attend all required study visits over approximately 3 months.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of neovascular (wet) AMD or other macular or retinal diseases, including epiretinal membrane (ERM) or diabetic retinopathy.
* Presence of geographic atrophy.
* Intolerability to MacuMira treatment.
* Baseline Rod Intercept Time (RIT) outside the eligibility range of 8.5 to 30 minutes.
* Presence of other ocular or systemic conditions that may confound central visual function (e.g., advanced glaucoma or optic neuritis) or study assessments (e.g., dementia).
